entry.title: Round Everything 1.0.0
entry.content:
Round Everything

Turns the taskbar into a frame around the whole screen. The taskbar keeps its rectangular shape, and the other three screen edges get a band of the same color, pushed inwards by a configurable offset. The visible "screen" becomes a rounded rectangle that sits flush against the taskbar, with one configurable corner radius.

Works with the taskbar on any edge (top, bottom, left, right) and on every monitor. A monitor without a taskbar ("Show my taskbar on all displays" off) gets the frame on all four edges.

How it works

The mod runs inside the taskbar's explorer.exe and creates one layered, always-on-top window per monitor covering the area next to the taskbar: three bands of the configured offset with the rounded corners. The taskbar itself, its background painted in the frame color, is the fourth side. The frame shape is drawn with GDI+ (anti-aliased); the inner area is fully transparent and lets the mouse through, while the painted frame is solid to the mouse, like the taskbar. No explorer function is hooked: the taskbar's XAML tree is reached through a few taskbar.dll symbol lookups (no XAML diagnostics, so it coexists with Taskbar Styler).

  • Color – the frame has one color of your choice, and the taskbar's own background (Taskbar.TaskbarBackground) is painted with it at the same opacity, so the taskbar and the frame are one surface. The taskbar's own background is restored when the mod is turned off.
  • Frame and taskbar come and go together. When the mod starts, the frame appears in the same instant as the taskbar's new look. When the taskbar moves, resizes or rebuilds (changing its position, a taskbar mod reloading) its background turns transparent and the frame goes away the instant the taskbar window moves; once everything has settled - taskbar at its new edge and uncloaked, its corners in place, the work area reserved - the taskbar paints its background again and, from inside that same rendering pass, reveals the frame (re-shaped for the new edge), so the two reach the screen in one composition. When the mod is turned off the frame disappears as the taskbar is handed back.
  • The frame stays visible during Aero Peek (hovering a taskbar thumbnail or the show-desktop corner), like the taskbar itself.
  • Task View (Win+Tab) – the frame goes away and the taskbar's background and monitor corners turn transparent while it is open; everything comes back together when it closes.
  • Full-screen apps – the frame hides on a monitor while a full-screen window (game, video, F11 browser) is showing there, and comes back afterwards.
  • Work area – Shrink the work area to the rounded screen (on by default) pushes the work area inwards so maximized and snapped windows stay inside the frame; turned off, the frame is purely visual: it overlaps the edges of maximized windows and lets the mouse through. Shrinking registers one invisible appbar per frame edge (the same mechanism the taskbar uses), so the shell reserves the space itself; the appbars are removed and the work area returns to normal when the option or the mod is turned off. Extra work-area inset shrinks it further, on all four sides, so a strip of wallpaper stays visible between the frame/taskbar and your windows.
  • Monitor corners – the four outer corners of each monitor are rounded too, so the whole screen reads as a rounded panel: the sliver outside a quarter circle is painted in the Monitor corner color (black by default). The two corners away from the taskbar are part of the frame itself; the two on the taskbar are XAML shapes added inside the taskbar (no extra windows, so nothing to fight over z-order with), click-through, removed when the mod is disabled.
  • Taskbar border line – the taskbar draws a 1px line along its inner edge (BackgroundStroke), which shows up as a seam between the taskbar and the frame. The mod sets that line's opacity to 0 and restores it when disabled.
  • Offsets and radii are in pixels at 100% scaling and scaled per monitor (configurable).

Window corners (dwm.exe)

Windows 11 rounds normal windows with a fixed 8 px radius and draws maximized windows square. With Round window corners on, the mod also runs inside dwm.exe and hooks the corner-radius decision (CTopLevelWindow::GetFloatCornerRadiusForCurrentStyle): every window that Windows would round - normal, snapped or maximized - gets the one Window corner radius you set, and maximized windows are rounded too, so they sit in the rounded screen like cards. Windows that opt out of rounding (DONOTROUND) and small-radius surfaces (menus, tooltips) are left alone. Changes apply at once: DWM is asked to re-evaluate every window (no window's own corner preference is touched). Full-screen windows share the maximized path in DWM, so they get rounded corners as well.

This part needs one manual step. Windhawk doesn't inject into dwm.exe by default (it is on Windhawk's list of critical system processes), so the window-corner part does nothing until you add dwm.exe to the Process inclusion list in Windhawk's advanced settings. The frame, the monitor corners and the work area don't depend on it and work right away. udwm.dll symbols are downloaded by Windhawk on first use.

This does the same job as the Rounded corners for maximized and snapped windows option of the Custom Window Corner Radius mod, through the same hook - the mechanism is the one Alexey Lavrinenko contributed there; use one mod or the other for window corners, not both.

Notes

  • Shell flyouts (Start, notification center, Task View, …) live above the frame, so they are never covered.
  • With the work area reserved, the frame is solid to the mouse, like the taskbar: clicks on it (and on the extra work-area inset strip) go nowhere, which keeps the invisible resize borders of maximized windows underneath from being hit. Without it the frame lets the mouse through.
  • With an auto-hide taskbar the frame spans the whole monitor and the taskbar slides in over it.
  • Setting all offsets to 0 and keeping a radius gives you just the rounded screen corners against the taskbar.

Credits

The taskbar-thread helpers (RunFromWindowThreadTimeout, FindCurrentProcessTaskbarWnd) and the taskbar.dll XAML-root lookup are ported from Taskbar multi-row by m417z, licensed under the GNU GPL v3.0. This mod is published under the same license.

entry.title: Desktop Window Cards 1.8.1
entry.content:
• Excluded programs: a blank entry hides the entries after it. Windhawk returns "" both for a blank array entry and past the end of the list, so the break on an empty entry ended the list at the first blank one. Every program listed after it stopped being excluded, with no warning. The loop now reads the bounded range (256 entries, only on start and on reload) and skips blank entries.
  • Excluded programs: normalization. \r/\n are trimmed along with spaces and quotes, / is accepted in full paths (C:/Program Files/...), and duplicate entries are ignored.
  • Worker: no busy loop on init failure. If the frame timer can't be created, handles[0] is null and MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx fails immediately, so the loop spins at 100% CPU. The worker now checks the window classes, controller and frame timer before it starts, logs which one failed, and leaves the loop on WAIT_FAILED.

THANKS TO @MayconDIS

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 1.1.1
entry.content:
• Panel position. A new Appearance option decides what stays centered while the details panel is open: the bar together with the panel (the bar slides left, the default) or the bar on its own (the panel opens to its right without moving it).
  • Solid is the new default background effect. A fresh install now starts with a plain, opaque colour instead of Acrylic. Anyone who already saved the settings keeps their choice. If the settings tab was never saved, the mod starts from the defaults, so the effect may change after this update.
  • Live acrylic is off by default, and it is a Windows 11 option. The live blur is drawn by Windows in a separate layer behind the bar, so while the details panel animates that layer can trail the bar by a frame and leave a slight seam at the edges. Off, the same effects come from a single snapshot taken when the bar opens: smoother and lighter on laptops. On Windows 10 the option is ignored and the snapshot is always used, because the compositor trails the most there.
  • The details panel wipes instead of fading in live mode. Windows cannot fade the blur layer, so the panel now animates its width with an opaque card: both layers are the same shape at every frame.
  • The last strip of the closing panel. Below a certain width Windows collapses the rounded blur layer into a minimum pill, which stayed on screen after the card had shrunk past it. The last few pixels are now drawn as a tinted tail that dissolves with the card, and the blur layer is hidden before it reaches that size.

entry.title: SnapSentry 0.23.0
entry.content:
• 0.23.0: The notification no longer leaves a Start Menu shortcut or a registry entry behind. SnapSentry's name and icon now come from a temporary entry that Windows discards at sign-out.
  • Windows keeps your notification banner and sound settings for SnapSentry when the mod is disabled or updated.
  • Screenshots are renamed as soon as they appear, before the popup, so other tools watching the folder see the final name right away.
  • Screenshots you keep are renamed too.

  • New "Name by time only" setting, which names each file with just the timestamp.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.0.0
entry.content:
Icons

  • A new Icons tab: a picture and a color for each of the island's icons, and 12 icon packs to download (Fluent, Lucide, Material, Phosphor, Emoji and more, with their licenses) or your own folder.

The island

  • "Hide as its line" can now hide it with the mouse away, while a window is maximized, or while a window is over it (Island style, #6068, #6532, #6798).
  • "Only the clock when hidden" (off by default, under "When it hides"): hidden by the auto-hide, a small pill with the time stays instead of the line, and turns into the line while an app's window is under it; the mouse on it opens the island (Island and Fixed styles, #6204). The Bar hidden with Win+J closes into the same pill (gone while a window is under it), and the mouse on it brings the bar back; hidden that way, new notifications follow "Banners even with the pill minimized".
  • "Fade the line after": the minimized line fades after 30 s, 2 min or 10 min (off by default), for OLED screens (#6525).
  • "Opens the line: With the mouse / With a click" (Hiding tab, the mouse by default; asked on Discord): with a click, the minimized line (and the hidden Bar's clock) only grows under the mouse and opens when clicked; it hides again when the mouse leaves, as before.
  • "Timer on the minimized line" (on by default, Hiding tab; asked on Discord): while a timer, Pomodoro or the stopwatch runs with the island minimized, the line becomes a small pill with the ring and time of the one ending first; with "Only the clock when hidden", the time goes beside the clock (not on the notches nor upright, where the line has no room).
  • With "Line that opens the island" on one notch, the other notches' lines are hidden and clicks there go to the windows below (#6468).
  • Notches in the Island style too (#6485): the same notches as the Fixed style, without keeping a strip (windows go under them). Each style keeps its own choice, so the Island style starts without notches and the Fixed style keeps its own.
  • "See-through bar" (off by default, Bar style): only the bar's items over what's behind it, or, with the frosted glass, only the blur with a light tint; with the opacity slider these are the bar's three looks asked for in #6109.
  • The bar on the left or the right side too (#6479): its items one under the other, its inner corners rounded (their size is a setting), the windows kept beside it.
  • The text size has its own slider, apart from the icons' size.
  • Win+J hides the whole bar in the Bar style too (#6519).
  • Profiles that turn on by themselves (#6166): in a profile's pencil, the apps that bring it once one stays in front a moment (the last app in front is one click away) and the styles; after its app, the island goes back to the profile before or stays.
  • A Reset button beside Export and Import (a double click) puts the island's settings back as they came; notes, tasks, events and profiles stay.
  • What's new rewritten for every version: each item says what it does and which tab has its option, and a click on it shows that option. An item with an option lights under the mouse, and a click anywhere on it shows that option.
  • "Light and shadow like macOS 27" (off by default, under Liquid Glass; an idea by Thiago Silva): the glass gets a sheen, a beveled edge, light along its bottom and a soft shadow, and the panels' cards look like glass too. It's drawn over Windows' own blur, so it shows in screenshots and recordings.
  • About shows Instagram's logo.

On the pill

  • "Your commands" (off by default): shortcuts to programs, files, folders, links or command lines, each with the icon of what it opens ("Choose..." picks a file); they're listed in their panel, and any of them can also be a button on the pill. Its form names each field and says what each kind does. Command lines run in a hidden job of their own (the 64-bit cmd.exe); one that fails shows a terminal. They're each Windows account's own (#6161, #6165, #6654).
  • "AI usage" (off by default, #6636): how much of the limits of Claude Code in a terminal and Codex is used, the one closer to its end with the time until it starts over (yellow from 70%, red from 90%), and both the 5-hour session and the week in its panel. It reads only what the agents keep on the PC (Codex's logs, and what Claude Code gives its status line, saved by a line the user adds to their status line's script): no login, token or network. The island never changes Claude Code's settings: its panel copies that line (for Git Bash or PowerShell), and the file it saves into is made first so only that Windows account can read it. The Claude desktop app doesn't leave its limits on the PC, so the option says it's the terminal one. Each agent shows with its installed app's icon.
  • The app in focus can show its window's title too (#6165).
  • A Caps Lock notice (an option, off by default, #6233).
  • Celsius or Fahrenheit for the weather (#6629, #6673).

Panels

  • A calendar card (off by default): the chosen day big beside the month (neighbor days dimmed, holidays in red, the week number), buttons for an alarm, a timer and the agendas, that day's events, and the upcoming events and holidays. The month its days show is named over them (a click on it goes back to today, #6165).
  • The weather's details as cards, like a phone's (off by default, #6129).
  • The control center changes the mobile hotspot's name and password; its mixer shows each volume in percent (#6160, #6537).
  • Pages opened straight from the pill have a back arrow (#6160).
  • The event editor says what its reminder does.
  • The weather can use your location ("Use my location" beside the city, asked on Discord): off until clicked, it uses Windows' own location permission ("Let desktop apps access your location"), on the weather's thread; refused or off, the city typed stays, and after a few times without a position the city typed shows meanwhile. The coordinates are rounded to about a kilometer before they go to Open-Meteo, and typing a city goes back to it.
  • Alarms have an optional name and the days they ring (asked on Discord): seven day buttons in the order of Windows' first day of the week; all of them is "Every day", none is "Once" (it turns itself off after ringing), and the list says "Weekdays", "Weekends" or the days. Alarms saved before ring every day.
  • "Brightness of external monitors (DDC/CI)" (on by default, Control center tab, #6502): off, nothing goes over the monitor's cable, for monitors that flicker or docks and MST hubs that reset when the control center opens; the built-in screen keeps Windows' own brightness.
  • On a monitor with HDR on, its brightness slider changes Windows' brightness of SDR content (the SDR white level), which is what the desktop shows, instead of the panel's DDC/CI level (#6700).

Notifications

  • Banners at a point of the screen (off by default): one of nine (the corners, the edges' middles or the center), in a window of their own sliding in from its edge; hover, buttons and replies work there as in the pill.
  • The banner's size (50% to 200%), width and corners.
  • "Calls and alarms silent in Do not disturb" (off by default): with it, calls, alarms and reminders don't ring either in the island's Do not disturb.

The dock

  • "When it hides" (Windhawk settings, Hiding and showing): "Mouse away" as before (the default), or "Window maximized" / "Window over it": the dock (or the transparent taskbar) stays up on the desktop and hides only while an app's window is maximized on its monitor, or is over it, or an app is full screen; the mouse at the bottom edge still brings it up (#6202, #6368, #6798). It's told by window events (SetWinEventHook), not by looking every few moments.
  • A width of its own (#6152): the dock stops at a width you choose, and the other apps scroll with the mouse wheel, like a box.
  • The magnification, the bounces and "When it hides" on the Windows taskbar kept as it is with only its apps too (an option there, #6167).

Files

  • A shelf (off by default, in the Desktop tab): files dropped anywhere on the pill (but on the folders' item) wait there, the newest first, 5 to 30 of them (10 by default, the oldest going). Its item shows how many; its panel lists them with thumbnails, to drag into another app (copied or moved as chosen for the folders panel), open, or take off one by one or all at once. Only their paths are kept, in the mod's storage.
  • Thumbnails of pictures, videos and documents in the folders panel and on the shelf (on by default), made on a thread; the mouse resting on one for half a second shows a bigger preview, like macOS' Quick Look.
  • A browser's download standing still for 30 s shows paused, in yellow (Edge, Chrome, Firefox, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi): browsers never tell the taskbar a download is paused.

Languages

  • Vietnamese (Tiếng Việt): the island's texts, What's new and the Windhawk settings, translated by @caotu2k5 in #6826 and completed for 3.0.

Settings

  • The settings window looks like Windows 11's: its own title bar on the Mica (with Windows' caption buttons and snap layouts), bigger texts, the small options two on a line in a wide window, a side bar as wide as the window allows, and scroll bars always shown, wider under the mouse and dragged like Windows' own (the side bar's too).
  • The mod's site, island.caliberda.com.br, in About: every option explained, the roadmap and votes. The mod's logo is on the settings window's title bar, its taskbar button and About.
  • The bubbles that ask or tell something (an option's needs, the icons' tips, the settings bubble) are opaque whatever the island's opacity.
  • A setup assistant (its own tab, under About) walks a new user through the main choices in six short steps: what the island is, the style, a ready-made set of pill items, hiding and notifications, the look (and how the dock is chosen in Windhawk), and a summary with links to each option. Each choice shows live and Cancel puts back what was there; it opens by itself only on a new install (never for an update), and its tab brings it back any time.
  • New tabs: Style (only what the chosen style has), Hiding (everything about the line, Win+J too), Control center and Banners; the loading bar moved to System, the Bar style's side, inner corners and items at the corners to Look, and the clock in the middle to Clock and calendar (the items' order stays the preview over every tab).
  • No choice cuts its names: each is measured, and the buttons go to more rows when they don't fit one.
  • The banners' place is picked on a little screen with its nine points; the bar's side, its inner corners and the banner's corners are drawn.
  • A dimmed option's reason opens a bubble with everything it needs (found by trying the changes in memory), as wide as its text; "Yes, change" makes them all at once and turns it on, and "Restore what changed" puts them back.
  • Files dragged out of the folders panel or the shelf: asked the first time or every time, or copied, or moved; the shelf asks like the folders panel.

Fixes

  • Alt or F10 in the settings window, or moving and sizing it, no longer stops the islands' animations until a click (Windows' menu mode); the settings window comes back on the main island after a restart when its monitor is gone.
  • The weather panel on another monitor's island no longer stays on "Searching" after a search or "Use my location".
  • With brightness through Windows only, a screen with HDR whose SDR brightness Windows refuses no longer hands its slider to the next screen.
  • An old custom icon without transparency on a pinned shortcut no longer shows as a black square in the dock.
  • "When it hides: window over it" looks at each monitor's own dock.
  • The Caps Lock bubble shows with three notches wherever the bell is; "Restore what changed" stays after the islands start again and leaves an option changed again since; the pill's shelf count follows files gone; a drop of only too long paths isn't said to be on the shelf.
  • The AI usage file (what Claude Code's status line saves) is each Windows account's own.
  • The dock keeps the icons set on the shortcuts pinned to the taskbar (changed in their properties) instead of the app's own (#6891).
  • With a monitor of another scale under the dock, the dock is no longer cut off center after its taskbar mode is switched (its icons' room measured in its own scale).
  • The tray icons of programs the island can't open (like NVIDIA's settings icon, from its display driver's service) keep their picture and show again after the mod is turned off and on (their program is asked to Windows by the process's ID).
  • With Windhawk run as administrator, the island gets the other apps' tray icons, the apps' badges and the download progress from the taskbar again, and notices when Explorer restarts (#6598); a tray icon's click then reaches only apps that aren't run as administrator.
  • With animations off, a panel opening from the pill no longer stretches the pill sideways for a few frames before it drops down, and the power button's confirmation shows.
  • Shortcuts and notes keep their line breaks with Windhawk portable (#6542).
  • Song lyrics for Apple Music (the app, Cider and its web page), whose artist comes with the album, and for players that don't tell a song's length (#6612).
  • Apps with notifications seen on one island (a notch or another monitor's) are seen on all of them.
  • No white band under the dock or the see-through taskbar after the taskbar hides by itself: the taskbar's own window is painted clear in those modes, also under its XAML.
  • With graphics drivers that can't make pictures smaller the smooth way (D2DERR_INTERMEDIATE_TOO_LARGE), the island turns that way off and draws again, instead of losing its frames (#6638).
  • In the Bar style with the clock in the middle, items no longer flash over the clock: an item whose side of the clock changes fades instead of sliding over it.
  • The Recycle Bin's count is watched again when Explorer starts after the island.
  • The bar moved to a side gives the screen's top back (and that side, when it moves again).
  • The dock comes up when the mouse slides along the bottom edge into it.
  • Changing the power mode or plan in the control center runs on a thread of its own: the island no longer freezes while Windows applies it (#6652).
  • Lyrics are looked for with players that don't tell a song's length, like Nagi (#6691); a log line says why a song gets none.
  • The places and icons per app go back to the general ones on the desktop and the taskbar, instead of staying the last app's (#6692).
  • Over another monitor below, the hidden dock slides away past the screen's edge like on the other monitors, instead of shrinking into a line above the edge: its window's room above the dock is higher there, so the window keeps more than half on its own monitor (its scale) with the whole dock past the edge.
  • With input methods that tell nothing when Shift switches their mode (the newest Microsoft Pinyin), the 中/英 item and its bubble follow it: the mode is asked every half second while a Chinese, Japanese or Korean keyboard is in front, from the window with the keyboard focus, and from Windows' text services when that window doesn't answer (#6460, #6422).
  • The control center's usage page reads CPU, RAM and VRAM by itself while it's open (it showed nothing without those items on the pill), and has CPU, RAM and VRAM tabs (#6790).
  • With two monitors, an island stays hidden while its own monitor has a full-screen window, whatever window has the focus (clicking the other monitor brought it back over a video); the dock's full-screen checks look at the monitor the same way (#6800).
  • A keyboard switched in the same app (Alt+Shift, Win+Space) shows on the island's language item: with two keyboards or more, the keyboard in front is read again every half second (newer Windows builds tell no event for it) (#6816).
  • A click on a notification of an unpackaged app (like Discord or other Electron apps) goes where the notification points, through the activator the app registered in its Start menu shortcut or in the registry, read on a thread of its own; before, only packaged apps' were found and the click only brought the app up (#6822).
  • The panels' corners follow the pill's corners setting (a square pill no longer opens into rounded panels), and the screenshot selection (Win+Shift+S) no longer counts as the app in front for the colors, places and profiles per app (#6609).
  • An app clicked in the dock bounces from the click until its window shows (up to the 6 s the dock waits for it), as "Bounce on launch" says, instead of only once its window was already there, over the new window and with the dock about to hide.
  • An app's own choice of icons ("Place and icons per app") kept before some items existed no longer shows those items while they're off for all apps (#6785, #6759).
  • The dock no longer turns the taskbar's auto-hide on while another app's auto-hide bar is on that edge (Windows answered with its "only one auto-hide toolbar per side" dialog); the log names that app.

entry.title: Windhawk UI Translator 0.1
entry.content:
Windhawk UI Translator

Windhawk localizes its own interface, but not the content mods write. This mod translates it in place, inside the Windhawk 2.0 window.

What it translates

Where What
Details page mod name, summary, README, changelog
Settings page titles, descriptions, tooltips, dropdown values and options, reset labels
Explore and installed lists mod names and one-line summaries

The Source tab and Windhawk's own interface strings are not translated.

Usage

Hover a translated block to see the original; on a touch screen, tap once for the original and again for the translation. Alt+Q (configurable) or a two-finger double-tap toggles translation.

Providers

Any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint is recommended; a glossary and batching are built in. Store its API key in Windows Credential Manager:

cmdkey /generic:windhawk-ui-translator /user:translator /pass:<your key>

The free Microsoft Edge endpoint needs no key and is the fallback; auto picks the LLM once a base URL and a key are configured. Google is not offered.

Notes

  • Enabled while the UI is already running, the mod does nothing until the UI process restarts: close and reopen Windhawk (windhawk-ui.exe), not just the tray icon.
  • The auto target language follows Windhawk's UI language, then the page or OS language (portable builds may not follow their own instance's); changes apply on the next page load or settings change.
  • If the UI fails to start: windhawk.exe -safe-mode, or windhawk-cli.exe mod disable windhawk-ui-translator.

Privacy

Page text goes to Microsoft's translation service by default, or to the configured LLM endpoint. No telemetry, no other network access. The API key is read from Windows Credential Manager and never reaches the page; the optional plaintext setting is the fallback, stored in Windhawk's own settings.

entry.title: WinTips OSD 1.2.1
entry.content:
WinTips OSD

A Windows 11 style floating overlay for the lock keys, Insert and clipboard actions. Nothing is injected into other programs and no system functions are hooked: it runs as a Windhawk tool mod in its own process.

Toggle Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock or press Insert and a small card slides in from the screen edge it sits closest to: a padlock icon that rotates and bounces, the state in words, and an accent bar along the bottom. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+X show a check mark or scissors with a ×N badge that counts consecutive actions.

Features

  • Real blurred backdrop. The card blurs whatever is behind it, the way the Windows 11 OSD does, while keeping a per-pixel-alpha window so the whole card can still fade and slide. Switch Card material to Solid for an opaque card.
  • Slides in from the nearest edge. A card within 15% of the left or right edge comes in horizontally (this wins over top/bottom), otherwise vertically from whichever half of the screen it sits in.
  • Clipboard aware. Copy tips only appear after the clipboard actually changes, so Ctrl+C used to interrupt a console app doesn't pop a false "Copied". Non-keyboard copies (context menu, in-app buttons) can be reported too.
  • Elevated apps. A 250 ms poll catches lock-key toggles made while an administrator window has focus, which a low-level keyboard hook can't see.
  • Follows Windows. Per-monitor DPI, light/dark theme and the system accent color.
  • Doesn't get in the way. Click-through, no focus stealing, not in the taskbar or Alt+Tab, fades out on its own.

Settings

  • Caps Lock / Num Lock / Scroll Lock / Insert / Copy / Paste / Cut — turn each tip on or off.
  • Also notify non-keyboard copies — context menu copies, in-app "Copy" buttons and any other clipboard change that wasn't made with Ctrl+C.
  • Display duration — how long the card stays, 500 to 10000 ms.
  • Animation speed — 100 is normal (300 ms), 50 is twice as fast, 0 disables the animation.
  • Vertical / horizontal position — above the taskbar or below the top edge; left, center or right.
  • Show on — the monitor that holds the mouse cursor, or always the primary display.
  • Horizontal / vertical offset — pixel-level fine tuning.
  • Theme — follow Windows, dark or light.
  • Card material — acrylic (blurred backdrop) or solid.
  • Blur radius — 0 to 40 pixels, acrylic material only.
  • Accent color — #RRGGBB for the status bar and the ×N badge; leave empty to follow the system accent color.
  • Detect toggles under elevated apps — the 250 ms poll described above (lock keys only).
  • Skip while a fullscreen app is in front — games, fullscreen video and presentation mode.

Things to know

  • Runs as a tool mod: it keeps working when Explorer restarts, and it never loads into other processes.
  • The standalone WinTips.exe does the same job. If it is already running, this mod stays quiet automatically, so both can be installed — but disable one of the two startup entries.
  • Insert is event-based: Windows doesn't keep a global Insert state.
  • The acrylic backdrop is a screen copy taken the moment the card appears. Behind an elevated window that copy can come back black, and the card falls back to solid for that tip instead of showing a black box.
  • Placement is preset based; fine positioning uses the offset settings.

Compared to Lock Keys Notifier

Lock Keys Notifier reports the same lock keys, so the overlap is worth spelling out. The two aim at different things:

  • Look. This mod reproduces the Windows 11 OSD: the card blurs the desktop behind it, slides in from the nearest edge and animates a padlock. Lock Keys Notifier draws a configurable toast on a solid background.
  • Scope. Clipboard tips have no equivalent there.
  • Configuration. Here the size, theme and material follow Windows on purpose. Lock Keys Notifier is built around being configurable — layouts, fonts, shadows, sounds, per-key accents — so it isn't trying to match the native OSD.

If you want lock keys only, and want to tune every pixel of the card, Lock Keys Notifier is the better fit. If you want the native Windows 11 look, or clipboard tips, this mod is.

Links

  • Standalone version, source and issue tracker: WinTips

entry.title: Copy File Contents 1.4
entry.content:
Copy File Contents

Adds two actions to File Explorer, so a file can be read without opening it:

  • Copy contents puts the text of the selected file on the clipboard.
  • Copy SHA-256 puts the hash of the selected file on the clipboard.

Several files can be selected at once. Contents are copied one after another with the file name above each, and hashes are copied one per line. A setting can put each file on the clipboard as its own item instead, which keeps them apart in Windows clipboard history, so Win+V offers each file on its own.

Two ways to reach it

Keyboard. Select files, then press Ctrl+Shift+T for the contents or Ctrl+Shift+H for the hash. This works with the new Windows 11 menu, because it does not go through the menu at all. The shortcut is only live while a File Explorer window has the focus and the file view is the one being pointed at, and it is ignored while the rename box, the address bar or the search box has the focus, so it never eats a letter you are typing. Every key combination here can be changed in the settings. Do not reuse Ctrl+Shift+C or Ctrl+Shift+N, which are File Explorer's own Copy as path and New folder, because the mod would take the key from Explorer.

Right-click. The two entries are also added to the classic menu, reached with Show more options or Shift+F10. They are added at the bottom of that menu, below Properties, and removed again once the menu closes, so the menu is never left modified. The new Windows 11 menu belongs to a different component and cannot be extended by injected code without registering a handler in the registry, which a mod must not do. To get the entries on a plain right-click, use the separate mod Classic context menu on Windows 11. If the classic menu cannot be reached on your build, the keyboard shortcuts are the whole of the mod and they do not need the menu at all.

What it will and will not copy

A file is copied only if it looks like text. Files that look binary are refused rather than pasted as garbage, and files larger than the size limit are refused the same way. When nothing at all could be copied, an optional prompt shows the reason. For an oversized local file up to 32 MB whose prefix looks like text, it offers to open it in Notepad instead. This prefix check is only a heuristic. Network and offline files are not opened for the offer. The path is passed quoted so a path with a space in it still opens.

The size limit is 8 MB by default, with the unit chosen next to it, megabytes or kilobytes. A large selection is copied file by file, so one file over the limit is skipped and the rest are still copied. That partial copy is silent, because a dialog in the middle of copying five files is worse than a missing one. When nothing at all can be copied, the optional prompt explains why instead.

The whole selection is also held to a 32 MB budget, so selecting a whole folder of logs cannot make File Explorer allocate without bound. A file bigger than what is left of that budget cannot fit in any encoding, so it is skipped without being opened, and once the budget is used up the rest of the selection is not read at all, which keeps a large Ctrl+A quick instead of slow. A file smaller than that is read and measured: its text is the same size on disk for UTF-16, and up to twice that for ASCII, so only the read itself can say.

The ceilings are 64 MB per file and 32 MB per selection whatever the settings say. In practice the per selection budget is the one that binds: no single file is copied beyond 32 MB of text, which is the same as saying that a 20 MB UTF-16 file is copied and a 20 MB ASCII file is not. A text file that big is already beyond what a clipboard is good for, and the mod refuses rather than trying.

When nothing in the selection can be copied, Copy contents is left out of the menu instead of being offered and then refusing. To decide that, the first 4 KiB of each file are read when the menu opens, stopping at the first file that passes, and looking at no more than 16 files. Files that are offline or stored online only are not read at all, because reading one would start a download; such a file is assumed copyable and the copy itself decides. Files on a network share are treated the same way, whether they are reached by a \\server\share path or through a drive letter mapped to one, because reading from a share that has stopped answering would hang the menu. A mixed selection still shows the entry and copies the files that can be copied.

Encoding is detected rather than assumed: a byte order mark is honored, then the file is checked for UTF-16 without a mark, then for strict UTF-8, and finally read as the system code page. UTF-16 is checked before UTF-8 on purpose: the zero bytes of a UTF-16 file are valid UTF-8, so the other order would decode such a file as text with invisible gaps. Line endings are copied as they are.

Large hashes

Hashing reads every byte, and the work runs on the same thread that owns the File Explorer window, so that window does not repaint until it is done. For a normal file that is instant; a gigabyte on a hard disk is about ten seconds. Above the size set in the settings, 256 MB by default, the mod asks first, and says how many files and how much data are involved, counting the whole selection rather than one file at a time. Answer no and nothing happens. The setting can be raised to where hashing a whole disk in one go is on you, or set to 0 to be asked every time.

Known limits

  • Only files. A selection of folders, or the desktop, does nothing.
  • The shortcuts act in File Explorer windows only. They do nothing in other programs and nothing on the desktop.
  • The contents are put on the clipboard as text. Nothing is written to disk, and no temporary file is created.
  • If the mod is turned off while its own prompt is open, the prompt is answered No for you and the copy stops, because the mod cannot be unloaded with its code still waiting on that dialog. Unloading waits about two seconds for work to finish. The wait between separate clipboard items ends as soon as unloading starts, but a single read from a share that has stopped answering cannot be interrupted, only waited out.
  • With separate clipboard items turned on, Ctrl+V pastes only the last file. The earlier ones are reachable through Windows clipboard history (Win+V), and only there, and clipboard history has to be turned on for them to be kept.
  • Clipboard history keeps 25 entries and about 4 MB per entry, which for text is roughly two million characters. A file bigger than that cannot be a history entry however it is copied; Windows drops it and tells no one. So in separate items mode those files are written last: the history keeps the files it can hold, and Ctrl+V gives the big one.
  • Windows clipboard history is a separate service and it needs a moment between copies, so the files are written with a short wait, 250 ms by default and adjustable. The wait runs on File Explorer's thread, so a large selection takes that much longer to finish copying, and the window is briefly unresponsive while it does.
  • A file being written by another program while it is read may be copied partially. That is a race no reader can win, and it is not worth a lock for this.

entry.title: MMC Dark Mode 1.0
entry.content:
MMC Dark Mode

A dark theme for the Microsoft Management Console: Device Manager, Services, Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, Disk Management and anything else hosted by mmc.exe.

Screenshots

Device Manager with the mod off:

Device Manager with the mod on:

What it does

The mod themes MMC windows in the mmc.exe process, including common trees, list views, property sheets and chrome. It also contains targeted handling for Services, Event Viewer, Task Scheduler and Disk Management. Existing menus and toolbars remain available. Some embedded content draws itself and is not themed.

Switching the mod off requests restoration of native styles, colours and painting. The system-wide colour table is not changed.

Known limits

  • MMC hosts many snap-ins and not every control or embedded page is covered. Layouts, visual styles and Windows builds may differ from those tested.
  • The Actions pane caption adjustment is x64-only and uses private DirectUI interfaces. If the required interfaces or hooks are unavailable, the native appearance is retained. Other custom-drawn content may remain light.
  • Disk Management's selected partition frame adjustment is x64-only and checks an exact native drawing-code signature. On an unknown or changed build it leaves that frame unchanged rather than guessing. The blue partition colour is adjusted only when the native renderer requests the observed stock navy. Any region or legend configured to that same navy will also be recoloured; other brush colours and native patterns are left unchanged.
  • The mod checks high contrast at load and does not activate when it is already enabled. Switching high contrast while MMC is running is not guaranteed to update every themed control; restart the console or disable the mod.
  • Some GDI brushes are deliberately retained until the MMC process exits because native controls may cache them. Repeatedly reloading the mod in the same process can increase GDI handle use.
  • The property-sheet tab strip is custom-painted; other tab layouts keep their native drawing. Push buttons generally keep native visuals, with a scoped dark face for the Task Scheduler summary Refresh button.
  • The maximized child window's menu-row buttons use scoped custom drawing. Other layouts may keep the native appearance. Restored child-window captions and their buttons can remain light.

entry.title: StartPad 1.0
entry.content:
StartPad

A macOS Launchpad-style fullscreen app launcher that replaces the Windows 11 Start menu, featuring horizontal paginated grids, interactive app folders, drag-and-drop reordering, and customizable visual themes.

Features & How to Use

Pages & Navigation

  • Horizontal Pages: Apps are organized into pages rather than a vertical scrolling list.
  • Switching Pages: Click and drag horizontally with the mouse, scroll the mouse wheel (vertical or horizontal), click the pagination dots at the bottom, or use Page Up / Page Down.
  • 2D Arrow Key Navigation: Use the Arrow keys or Tab to move selection across icons. Moving past the left or right edge of the grid automatically flips to the previous or next page.

Drag-and-Drop & Folders

  • Reorder Apps: Click and hold (~320 ms) on any app or folder icon to pick it up, then drag it to a new position on the grid or across pages (hold near the screen edge to flip pages).
  • Create Folders:
    • Drag & Drop: Drag one app icon directly onto another app icon (or into an existing folder).
    • Selection Mode: Click the More (...) button on the right side of the search bar and choose Create folder, click the apps you want to bundle (marked with a blue checkmark), and click the Done (✓) button in the search bar (or press Enter).
  • Rename Folders: When a folder is open, click its title at the top or press F2 (also works when a folder is selected on the main grid), type the new name, and press Enter.
  • Remove or Ungroup: Drag an icon outside the open folder panel to move it back to the main grid, or right-click a folder and select Ungroup folder.
  • Persistent Layout: Your custom icon order, folders, and hidden apps are automatically saved to Windhawk's mod storage per user.

Search & Launching

  • Instant Search: Start typing anywhere to filter apps immediately. Press Esc or click the clear (×) button to reset the search.
  • Launch App: Click an icon or press Enter on the selected app.
  • Run as Administrator: Hold Ctrl + Shift + Enter on a selected app, or right-click the app and choose Run as administrator.
  • Context Menu: Right-click any app to Open, Run as administrator, Open file location, Remove from folder, or Hide.

More Options (...) & Hiding Apps

Click the ... button inside the right side of the search bar to access:

  • Create folder: Interactively select multiple apps to group into a new folder.
  • Edit hidden apps: Toggle visibility badges on all apps to hide or unhide multiple items at once, then click the Done (✓) button in the search bar to save.
  • Search in hidden apps: When checked, typing a search query will also return matching apps that you have hidden.
  • Reset layout: Restores the default alphabetical layout and removes all custom folders and hidden-app rules.

Power Menu & Visuals

  • Power Button: Located at the bottom right (aligned with the page dots and last column), providing quick access to Lock, Sign out, Sleep, Shut down, and Restart.
  • Visual Styles: Choose between MacOS Style (pill search bar & squircle folders) and Windows 11 Fluent (Acrylic-inspired search box with system accent bar), automatically adapting to Windows Light and Dark modes.
  • Legacy Icon Cleanup: Automatically detects and removes the thin 1px border frame Windows adds around small legacy Win32 icons (such as 7-Zip) and smoothly upscales them.
  • Localized UI: Built-in translations for English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

How StartPad differs from "fullscreen-start" mod

Both mods replace the Start menu with a fullscreen app launcher, and they cannot be enabled at the same time because both intercept XamlLauncher::ShowStartView.

  • StartPad focuses on a paginated macOS Launchpad workflow: horizontal pages with spring physics, folders (creation, renaming, ungrouping), drag-and-drop icon reordering with persistent layout storage, hiding apps, a right-click context menu (Run as administrator, Open file location), an integrated Power menu, a Windows 11 Fluent visual style, and multilingual UI strings.
  • Fullscreen Start (fullscreen-start) by Rafael Mendes focuses on a single vertically scrolled grid with Direct2D rendering, live DWM Acrylic/Blur backdrops, Ctrl+V clipboard paste in search, keeping the taskbar visible, and integration with the Standalone Dock mod.

Credits & License

  • Hooking XamlLauncher::ShowStartView in twinui.pcshell.dll (kShowMethodKeyboard / kShowFlagKeyboard), secondary folder-process detection (IsFolderWindowsProcess), and thread initialization/uninitialization structure are adapted from Fullscreen Start (Launchpad style) (fullscreen-start) by Rafael Mendes, licensed under the MIT License (Copyright (c) Rafael Mendes).
  • Licensed under the MIT License.

entry.title: Hourly Peek Buddy 1.0
entry.content:
Hourly Peek Buddy

A fun reminder for the top of every hour or at the times you choose.

A funny little character pops up from the bottom corner of your screen, waves at you with a speech bubble, and goes away again. It shows up at the top of every hour and at any other times you choose, and it appears on top of all your apps. There are 14 characters and 6 ways of showing up, and you can see the result right away with the built-in preview, so you never have to wait for the next hour.

All characters are drawn by the mod itself, so there are no images to download.

Preview

Windhawk settings cannot have a button, so the preview works like this:

  • Preview when settings are saved (on by default): every time you press Save, the character shows up once with your new settings.
  • Preview now: flip this switch and save, and the character shows up again even if nothing else has changed.

Tip: pick a character or a movement, save, and watch. Repeat until you find your favorite.

Characters

Ghost, Cat, Alien, Robot, Penguin (with a party hat), Duck, Slime, Grumpy bomb, Cactus, Pumpkin, Teddy bear, Mushroom, Donut and Pizza slice. Or choose Random to be surprised every time.

Ways of showing up

  • Peek: Rises from the bottom edge and wiggles.
  • Springy: Pops up like a jack-in-the-box and bounces.
  • Slide: Slides in from the side of the screen with a little overshoot.
  • Hop: Hops in from the side of the screen.
  • Spin: Flies in from the corner while spinning.
  • Pop: Grows out of the corner with a bounce.

When does it show up?

  • At the top of every hour (can be turned off).
  • Every N minutes, counted from midnight (for example 15 means :00, :15, :30 and :45; 0 turns this off).
  • At exact times of your choice, for example 09:30, 13:15, 17:45.
  • Quiet hours: it stays away between the two hours you choose (for example from 23 to 8). Using the same value for both turns quiet hours off.
  • Optional: skip it while a full-screen game, video or presentation is active.

Settings

  • Preview when settings are saved / Preview now
  • Character, Movement, Corner (bottom right or bottom left), Monitor (primary or the one with the mouse)
  • Schedule: top of every hour, every N minutes, exact times, quiet hours
  • Stay time (seconds), Size (%), Opacity (%)
  • Speech bubble: time with a funny message, time only, your own message ({time} is replaced with the current time), or no bubble
  • Message language: automatic (follows Windows), Turkish or English
  • Click to dismiss, Play a sound, Skip full-screen apps

Notes

  • The mod runs in its own windhawk.exe process and does not inject into other programs. It does not change any system or registry setting.
  • The character window never takes the keyboard focus. If Click to dismiss is off, the character is click-through and the mouse goes straight to the app below.
  • The size follows the DPI of the monitor.
  • It appears above the taskbar edge (the work area), as if it peeks out from behind it.
  • If you start a new show (for example with the preview) while one is on the screen, the old one is replaced.

Saat Başı Sürpriz Dostu

Ekranın alt köşesinden komik, küçük bir karakter çıkar, konuşma balonuyla size göz kırpar ve tekrar gider. Her saat başı ve seçtiğiniz diğer zamanlarda ortaya çıkar, üstelik tüm uygulamaların üzerinde görünür. 14 karakter ve 6 farklı çıkış şekli vardır; yerleşik ön izleme sayesinde sonucu hemen görürsünüz, bir sonraki saat başını beklemenize gerek kalmaz.

Tüm karakterleri modun kendisi çizer, bu yüzden indirilecek görsel yoktur.

Ön izleme

Windhawk ayarlarında düğme olamadığı için ön izleme şöyle çalışır:

  • Ayarlar kaydedilince ön izle (varsayılan olarak açık): Kaydet'e her bastığınızda karakter, yeni ayarlarınızla bir kez ortaya çıkar.
  • Şimdi ön izle: Bu anahtarı çevirip kaydederseniz, başka hiçbir şey değişmemiş olsa bile karakter yeniden çıkar.

İpucu: Bir karakter veya hareket seçin, kaydedin ve izleyin. Favorinizi bulana kadar tekrarlayın.

Karakterler

Hayalet, Kedi, Uzaylı, Robot, Penguen (parti şapkalı), Ördek, Jöle, Huysuz bomba, Kaktüs, Balkabağı, Oyuncak ayı, Mantar, Donut ve Pizza dilimi. Her seferinde sürpriz için Rastgele'yi seçebilirsiniz.

Çıkış şekilleri

  • Dikizleme: Alt kenardan yükselir ve sallanır.
  • Yaylı: Kutudan fırlayan oyuncak gibi çıkar ve zıplar.
  • Kayma: Ekranın kenarından hafif taşarak kayarak gelir.
  • Hoplama: Ekranın kenarından hoplaya hoplaya gelir.
  • Dönme: Köşeden dönerek uçarak gelir.
  • Patlama: Köşeden zıplayarak büyür.

Ne zaman çıkar?

  • Her saat başı (kapatılabilir).
  • Her N dakikada bir, geceyarısından itibaren sayılır (örneğin 15 için :00, :15, :30 ve :45; 0 bunu kapatır).
  • Seçtiğiniz tam saatlerde, örneğin 09:30, 13:15, 17:45.
  • Sessiz saatler: Seçtiğiniz iki saat arasında çıkmaz (örneğin 23 ile 8 arası). İkisine de aynı değeri vermek sessiz saatleri kapatır.
  • İsteğe bağlı: Tam ekran oyun, video veya sunum varken atlanır.

Ayarlar

  • Ayarlar kaydedilince ön izle / Şimdi ön izle
  • Karakter, Hareket, Köşe (sağ alt veya sol alt), Monitör (ana monitör veya fare imlecinin olduğu monitör)
  • Zamanlama: her saat başı, her N dakikada bir, tam saatler, sessiz saatler
  • Kalma süresi (saniye), Boyut (%), Opaklık (%)
  • Konuşma balonu: saat ve komik mesaj, sadece saat, kendi mesajınız ({time} yerine o anki saat yazılır) veya balonsuz
  • Mesaj dili: otomatik (Windows'u izler), Türkçe veya İngilizce
  • Tıklayınca kapat, Ses çal, Tam ekran uygulamaları atla

Notlar

  • Mod kendi windhawk.exe sürecinde çalışır ve başka programlara kod enjekte etmez. Hiçbir sistem veya kayıt defteri ayarını değiştirmez.
  • Karakter penceresi klavye odağını almaz. Tıklayınca kapat kapalıysa karakter tıklamayı geçirir; fare doğrudan alttaki uygulamaya gider.
  • Boyut, monitörün DPI değerini izler.
  • Karakter görev çubuğunun kenarının (çalışma alanının) üstünde, sanki arkasından dikiliyormuş gibi görünür.
  • Ekranda bir karakter varken yenisi başlatılırsa (örneğin ön izleme ile) eskisinin yerini alır.

entry.title: Mouse Cursor Themes 1.0
entry.content:
Mouse Cursor Themes

Replaces the Windows mouse cursors with a theme of your choice. All cursors are drawn by the mod itself, so every theme is available right after you enable the mod and you can switch themes from the settings at any time.

The mod draws cursor files for the theme and replaces the system cursors of your current Windows session with them. It does not change your saved pointer scheme or any registry settings. Because of this, the theme works in every program that uses the standard Windows cursors.

Preview

Themes

  • Classic White: White arrow with a black outline.
  • Classic Black: Black arrow with a white outline.
  • Neon Blue / Neon Pink / Neon Green: Bright outline with a glowing halo.
  • Sunset: Orange to pink gradient with a soft warm glow.
  • Ocean: Aqua to deep blue gradient.
  • Gold: Golden gradient with a dark brown outline.
  • Rainbow: A rainbow-colored cursor.
  • Crimson: Red cursor with a white outline and a red glow.
  • Silver: Metallic silver gradient with a dark outline.
  • Forest: Light green to deep green gradient with a dark green outline.
  • Lava: Yellow to red-orange gradient with a hot orange glow.
  • Lavender: Soft lilac to purple gradient.
  • Aurora: Mint to violet gradient with a cool glow.
  • Ice: White to icy blue gradient with a blue outline.
  • Candy: Pink to sky blue gradient with a white outline.
  • Midnight: Dark navy cursor with a golden outline and glow.
  • Ghost: Only an outline, the inside is transparent.
  • Custom: Pick your own fill, outline and glow colors.

Pointer shapes

The shape of the main pointer can be changed independently from the theme. The same shape is also used by the busy (working in background) and help cursors. Shapes marked "tip" click with their tip, the others click at their center.

  • Classic arrow: The standard Windows arrow (tip).
  • Arrowhead: The classic arrow without its stem (tip).
  • Triangle: A plain triangle (tip).
  • Wedge: A slim triangle with a straight left edge (tip).
  • Kite: A kite shape (tip).
  • Navigator: A sharp navigation-style arrowhead (tip).
  • Chevron: Two strokes forming an open corner (tip).
  • Diamond / Square / Dot / Ring / Target: Simple geometric shapes.
  • Star / Sparkle / Heart: Decorative shapes.

Cursors that are replaced

Normal arrow, text (I-beam), link (hand), busy (animated), working in background (animated), precision cross, up arrow, all resize cursors, move, unavailable (forbidden) and help.

Settings

  • Theme
  • Pointer shape: Shape of the main pointer (see above).
  • Cursor size (%): 100 matches the original Windows cursor size.
  • Glow (%): Makes the glow of the themes weaker or stronger (0 turns it off).
  • Outline thickness (%): Makes the outline of the cursor thinner or thicker. A thicker outline is easier to see.
  • Crisp edges: Draws sharper, less blurry cursor edges.
  • Contrast edge: Adds a thin dark or light line around the outline, so the cursor stays clearly visible on any background.
  • Animated busy cursors: Turns the spinning busy cursors on or off.
  • Custom colors: Used only when the "Custom" theme is selected (format: #RRGGBB).

Notes

  • The cursor size follows the Windows pointer size setting (Settings > Accessibility > Mouse pointer and touch). The cursors are drawn in several sizes, so they stay sharp.
  • The mod never changes your saved pointer scheme. When you disable the mod, Windows reloads your own pointer scheme. The replaced cursors only live in memory, so after you sign out they return to your pointer scheme until the mod is started again.
  • Programs that use their own cursors (for example some games and drawing programs) keep their own cursors.
  • If you change the pointer scheme from the Windows settings while the mod is running, the mod notices it and applies the theme again.
  • The generated cursor files are kept in Windhawk's storage folder for this mod and are removed when the mod is disabled.

Fare İmleci Temaları

Windows fare imleçlerini seçtiğiniz bir temayla değiştirir. Tüm imleçler modun kendisi tarafından çizilir; bu yüzden modu açtığınız anda bütün temalar hazırdır ve ayarlardan istediğiniz zaman tema değiştirebilirsiniz.

Mod, tema için imleç dosyaları çizer ve geçerli Windows oturumunuzun sistem imleçlerini bu dosyalarla değiştirir. Kayıtlı işaretçi şemanızı veya kayıt defteri ayarlarını değiştirmez. Bu sayede tema, standart Windows imleçlerini kullanan her programda çalışır.

Temalar

  • Klasik Beyaz: Siyah çerçeveli beyaz ok.
  • Klasik Siyah: Beyaz çerçeveli siyah ok.
  • Neon Mavi / Neon Pembe / Neon Yeşil: Parlak çerçeve ve ışıldayan halo.
  • Gün Batımı: Turuncudan pembeye geçişli, yumuşak sıcak parıltılı.
  • Okyanus: Açık turkuazdan koyu maviye geçişli.
  • Altın: Koyu kahverengi çerçeveli altın renkli geçiş.
  • Gökkuşağı: Gökkuşağı renklerinde imleç.
  • Kızıl: Beyaz çerçeveli, kırmızı parıltılı kırmızı imleç.
  • Gümüş: Koyu çerçeveli, metalik gümüş geçişli.
  • Orman: Açık yeşilden koyu yeşile geçişli, koyu yeşil çerçeveli.
  • Lav: Sarıdan kırmızı-turuncuya geçişli, sıcak turuncu parıltılı.
  • Lavanta: Yumuşak leylaktan mora geçişli.
  • Aurora: Naneden menekşeye geçişli, serin parıltılı.
  • Buz: Beyazdan buz mavisine geçişli, mavi çerçeveli.
  • Şeker: Pembeden gök mavisine geçişli, beyaz çerçeveli.
  • Gece Yarısı: Koyu lacivert, altın sarısı çerçeveli ve parıltılı.
  • Hayalet: Sadece çerçeve, içi şeffaf.
  • Özel: Dolgu, çerçeve ve parıltı renklerini kendiniz seçersiniz.

İşaretçi şekilleri

Ana işaretçinin şekli temadan bağımsız olarak değiştirilebilir. Aynı şekil, meşgul (arka planda çalışıyor) ve yardım imleçlerinde de kullanılır. "uç" yazan şekiller uç noktalarıyla, diğerleri merkezleriyle tıklar.

  • Klasik ok: Standart Windows oku (uç).
  • Ok başı: Klasik okun çubuksuz hâli (uç).
  • Üçgen: Sade bir üçgen (uç).
  • Kama: Sol kenarı düz, ince bir üçgen (uç).
  • Uçurtma: Uçurtma biçimi (uç).
  • Pusula oku: Keskin, navigasyon tarzı ok başı (uç).
  • Köşe: Açık bir köşe oluşturan iki çizgi (uç).
  • Elmas / Kare / Nokta / Halka / Hedef: Sade geometrik şekiller.
  • Yıldız / Parıltı / Kalp: Süslü şekiller.

Değiştirilen imleçler

Normal ok, metin (I imleci), bağlantı (el), meşgul (animasyonlu), arka planda çalışıyor (animasyonlu), hassas artı, yukarı ok, tüm boyutlandırma imleçleri, taşıma, kullanılamaz (yasak) ve yardım.

Ayarlar

  • Tema
  • İşaretçi şekli: Ana işaretçinin şekli (yukarıya bakın).
  • İmleç boyutu (%): 100, orijinal Windows imleç boyutuna denk gelir.
  • Parıltı (%): Temaların parıltısını azaltır veya artırır (0 kapatır).
  • Çerçeve kalınlığı (%): İmlecin çerçevesini inceltir veya kalınlaştırır. Kalın çerçeve imleci daha kolay görünür yapar.
  • Keskin kenarlar: İmleç kenarlarını daha keskin, daha az bulanık çizer.
  • Kontrast kenarı: Çerçevenin etrafına ince bir koyu veya açık çizgi ekler; böylece imleç her arka planda net görünür.
  • Animasyonlu meşgul imleçleri: Dönen meşgul imleçlerini açar veya kapatır.
  • Özel renkler: Sadece "Özel" tema seçiliyse kullanılır (biçim: #RRGGBB).

Notlar

  • İmleç boyutu Windows'un işaretçi boyutu ayarını izler (Ayarlar > Erişilebilirlik > Fare işaretçisi ve dokunma). İmleçler birkaç boyutta çizildiği için net kalır.
  • Mod kayıtlı işaretçi şemanızı hiçbir zaman değiştirmez. Modu kapattığınızda Windows kendi işaretçi şemanızı yeniden yükler. Değiştirilen imleçler yalnızca bellekte bulunur; oturumu kapattığınızda mod yeniden başlayana kadar işaretçi şemanıza döner.
  • Kendi imleçlerini kullanan programlar (örneğin bazı oyunlar ve çizim programları) kendi imleçlerini korur.
  • Mod çalışırken Windows ayarlarından işaretçi şemasını değiştirirseniz mod bunu fark eder ve temayı yeniden uygular.
  • Oluşturulan imleç dosyaları, Windhawk'ın bu mod için ayırdığı depolama klasöründe tutulur ve mod kapatılınca silinir.

entry.title: AI Voice Typing 1.0.0
entry.content:
AI Voice Typing

English | Português | Español

Press a shortcut, speak, press it again, and your words are typed where the cursor is, in any app. An AI transcribes what you said and cleans it up in the style you choose, or translates it. It uses a cloud provider you set up with your own key: Groq is recommended (very fast, and its key is free).

What it does

  • Dictation in any app. A small bar at the bottom of the screen shows what you're saying while you speak. When you stop, the text is pasted where you were typing and also left on the clipboard. Dictating again right after, in the same field, adds the space between the two.
  • Cleaned up in your style. The AI removes the "ums", repetitions and false starts, and fixes punctuation, without changing what you said. Styles: Natural, Professional, Prompt (for writing to an AI), Raw and Transcript only, plus your own. Each app can have its own style (Outlook always Professional, VS Code always Prompt).
  • Translation. Ctrl+Shift+Y dictates and translates, to one of 34 languages.
  • The result card. After each dictation, a card shows the text. Its chips redo it in another style or translate it, and Replace swaps the pasted text for the new version.
  • Command. Select text in any app, press Ctrl+Alt+K and say what to do with it ("more formal", "translate to Spanish", "summarize as bullets"). The result replaces the selection.
  • About 100 languages to speak in, detected by itself or chosen. The settings and the bar are in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Japanese, Chinese, Russian, Hindi and Bengali.
  • Several providers: Groq, Google Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, OpenAI, or an OpenAI-compatible server. With more than one set up, the next one is tried when one fails. If the transcription still fails, the recording is kept so you can try again without speaking it all again.

Getting started

  1. Create a free key at console.groq.com/keys (or at another provider: the settings show how, step by step).
  2. The first time, a short setup wizard opens: the look, the provider (paste the key and it's tested at once), the shortcut and style, and a test dictation. It can be done again from General.
  3. Click any text field, press Ctrl+Shift+Space, speak, and press it again (or click the bar's stop button).
Shortcut What it does
Ctrl+Shift+Space Dictate (press again to stop; in hold mode, hold it while you speak)
Ctrl+Shift+Y Dictate and translate
Ctrl+Alt+K Command on the selected text (while you speak, the card also offers the styles, to apply one without speaking)
Esc Cancel while recording (while it's being processed, the bar's ✕ cancels)

Every shortcut can be changed in the settings. "Paste again" (the last dictation into the app in front) and "Dictate now" are in the icon's menu; "Paste again" has no shortcut by default, because Ctrl+Alt+V is Office's Paste Special.

Settings

Click the mod's icon in the notification area to open them (right-click it for a quick menu): this session's history (with "Redo" in another style or language), the styles and your own ones, a style per app, the providers (keys, models and the order they're tried in), the shortcuts, the spoken language, microphone and dictionary, and the look: theme, accent color, the card's width and a glass look for the bar. Start and stop sounds are on by default and can be turned off.

Privacy

  • The audio goes only to the speech provider you set up (for example Groq, api.groq.com), and only with a key saved: while you speak (the live preview, which can be turned off) and when you stop. The transcript then goes to the text provider for the style or the translation, along with the name of the app you're typing into (so the text fits it) and the words in your dictionary. With Command, the selected text goes too. Each provider's own privacy policy applies (on Gemini's free tier, Google may use what's sent to improve its products).
  • If Groq answers that the chosen model no longer exists, the mod asks Groq for its current list of models, tries up to 4 of them with a short test (a second of near-silence, or "OK"), and keeps the one that works.
  • Servers contacted, only those of the providers you set up: api.groq.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Gemini), openrouter.ai, api.mistral.ai, api.openai.com, or the address you give for an OpenAI-compatible server.
  • Nothing is saved to disk: the audio, the text and the history stay in memory. A recording whose transcription failed also stays only in memory (the last 3), until it's tried again or the history is cleared.
  • The dictated text is left on the clipboard, like a normal copy. Command copies the selection with Ctrl+C and then puts your clipboard back as it was.
  • Your keys are stored encrypted for your Windows account (DPAPI), in the mod's own storage, and are removed with the mod.

Known limitations

  • Windows doesn't let a normal app type into apps running as administrator: there, the text is only copied (paste it with Ctrl+V), and Command can't read the selection.
  • Command doesn't work in terminals (Ctrl+C stops the program there).
  • Ctrl+Alt is AltGr on many keyboards: where AltGr+K types a character (for example Hungarian or Czech), Command starts without a shortcut; choose one in the settings.
  • The glass look needs Windows' transparency effects (with them off, or with the energy saver on, the bar stays solid).
  • Cloud providers only (no local models), over https, so it needs an internet connection. The OpenAI-compatible server is used for the text, not for speech.
  • A recording stops by itself after 12 minutes and is transcribed (the providers take files of about 13 minutes at most).

Prefer a standalone app with more options? The same author makes FlowVoice.

Contact and support

Made in Brazil by caliberda. Bugs: please open an issue on GitHub (that's where they're tracked). If the mod helps you, you can support it on GitHub Sponsors. Instagram: @cesar.kali · caliberda.com.br

Português

Aperte um atalho, fale, aperte de novo, e suas palavras são digitadas onde está o cursor, em qualquer app. Uma IA transcreve o que você disse e limpa no estilo que você escolher, ou traduz. Ela usa um provedor na nuvem que você configura com a sua própria chave: a Groq é a recomendada (muito rápida, e a chave é grátis).

O que faz

  • Ditado em qualquer app. Uma barrinha embaixo da tela mostra o que você está falando enquanto fala. Quando você para, o texto é colado onde você estava digitando e também fica na área de transferência. Ditando de novo logo em seguida, no mesmo campo, o espaço entre os dois entra sozinho.
  • Limpo no seu estilo. A IA tira os "hã", "né", repetições e frases começadas de novo, e acerta a pontuação, sem mudar o que você disse. Estilos: Natural, Profissional, Prompt (para escrever para uma IA), Cru e Só transcrição, e os seus. Cada app pode ter o seu estilo (Outlook sempre Profissional, VS Code sempre Prompt).
  • Tradução. Ctrl+Shift+Y dita e traduz, para um de 34 idiomas.
  • O card do resultado. Depois de cada ditado, um card mostra o texto. Os chips refazem em outro estilo ou traduzem, e Substituir troca o texto colado pela versão nova.
  • Comando. Selecione um texto em qualquer app, aperte Ctrl+Alt+K e diga o que fazer ("mais formal", "traduz pro inglês", "resume em tópicos"). O resultado substitui a seleção.
  • Cerca de 100 idiomas para falar, detectados sozinhos ou escolhidos. As configurações e a barra estão em português, inglês, espanhol, francês, alemão, japonês, chinês, russo, hindi e bengali.
  • Vários provedores: Groq, Google Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, OpenAI ou um servidor compatível com a OpenAI. Com mais de um, o próximo é tentado quando um falha. Se a transcrição ainda assim falhar, a gravação fica guardada para tentar de novo sem falar tudo outra vez.

Como começar

  1. Crie uma chave grátis em console.groq.com/keys (ou em outro provedor: as configurações mostram o passo a passo).
  2. Na primeira vez, abre um assistente rápido: a aparência, o provedor (cole a chave e ela é testada na hora), o atalho e o estilo, e um ditado de teste. Dá para refazer em Geral.
  3. Clique em qualquer campo de texto, aperte Ctrl+Shift+Espaço, fale e aperte de novo (ou clique no botão de parar da barra).
Atalho O que faz
Ctrl+Shift+Espaço Ditar (aperte de novo para parar; no modo segurar, segure enquanto fala)
Ctrl+Shift+Y Ditar e traduzir
Ctrl+Alt+K Comando no texto selecionado (enquanto você fala, o card também oferece os estilos, para aplicar um sem falar)
Esc Cancela durante a gravação (enquanto processa, o ✕ da barra cancela)

Todos os atalhos podem ser trocados nas configurações. "Colar de novo" (o último ditado no app da frente) e "Ditar agora" ficam no menu do ícone; "Colar de novo" não tem atalho por padrão, porque Ctrl+Alt+V é o Colar especial do Office.

Configurações

Clique no ícone do mod na área de notificação para abri-las (com o botão direito, um menu rápido): o histórico desta sessão (com "Refazer" em outro estilo ou idioma), os estilos e os seus, um estilo por app, os provedores (chaves, modelos e a ordem de tentativa), os atalhos, o idioma falado, o microfone e o dicionário, e a aparência: tema, cor de destaque, largura do card e o visual de vidro da barra. Os sons de início e fim vêm ligados e dá para desligar.

Privacidade

  • O áudio vai só para o provedor de voz que você configurou (por exemplo a Groq, api.groq.com) e só com uma chave salva: enquanto você fala (a prévia ao vivo, que dá para desligar) e quando você para. A transcrição então vai ao provedor de texto para o estilo ou a tradução, junto com o nome do app em que você está digitando (para o texto combinar com ele) e as palavras do seu dicionário. No Comando, o texto selecionado vai junto. Vale a política de privacidade de cada provedor (no plano grátis do Gemini, o Google pode usar o que é enviado para melhorar os produtos dele).
  • Se a Groq responder que o modelo escolhido não existe mais, o mod pede à Groq a lista atual de modelos, testa até 4 deles com um teste curto (um segundo de quase silêncio, ou "OK") e fica com o que funcionar.
  • Servidores contatados, só os dos provedores que você configurou: api.groq.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Gemini), openrouter.ai, api.mistral.ai, api.openai.com, ou o endereço que você informar para um servidor compatível com a OpenAI.
  • Nada é gravado em disco: o áudio, o texto e o histórico ficam na memória. Uma gravação cuja transcrição falhou também fica só na memória (as 3 últimas), até ser tentada de novo ou o histórico ser limpo.
  • O texto ditado fica na área de transferência, como uma cópia normal. O Comando copia a seleção com Ctrl+C e depois devolve a sua área de transferência como estava.
  • As chaves são guardadas criptografadas para a sua conta do Windows (DPAPI), no armazenamento do próprio mod, e são apagadas junto com ele.

Limitações conhecidas

  • O Windows não deixa um app comum digitar em apps abertos como administrador: neles, o texto só é copiado (cole com Ctrl+V), e o Comando não consegue ler a seleção.
  • O Comando não funciona em terminais (lá o Ctrl+C interrompe o programa).
  • Ctrl+Alt é o AltGr em muitos teclados: onde AltGr+K digita um caractere (por exemplo húngaro ou tcheco), o Comando começa sem atalho; escolha um nas configurações.
  • O vidro precisa dos efeitos de transparência do Windows (desligados, ou com a economia de energia, a barra fica sólida).
  • Só provedores na nuvem (sem modelos locais), por https, então precisa de internet. O servidor compatível com a OpenAI é usado para o texto, não para a voz.
  • Uma gravação para sozinha depois de 12 minutos e é transcrita (os provedores aceitam arquivos de uns 13 minutos no máximo).

Prefere um app separado com mais opções? O mesmo autor faz o FlowVoice.

Contato e apoio

Feito no Brasil por caliberda. Bugs: abra uma issue no GitHub (é lá que eles são acompanhados). Se o mod te ajuda, dá para apoiar pelo GitHub Sponsors ou por Pix no LivePix. Instagram: @cesar.kali · caliberda.com.br

Español

Pulsa un atajo, habla, vuelve a pulsarlo y tus palabras se escriben donde está el cursor, en cualquier app. Una IA transcribe lo que dijiste y lo limpia en el estilo que elijas, o lo traduce. Usa un proveedor en la nube que configuras con tu propia clave: se recomienda Groq (muy rápido, y la clave es gratis).

  • Dictado en cualquier app, con una barra pequeña que muestra lo que dices mientras hablas. El texto se pega donde escribías y también queda en el portapapeles.
  • Limpio en tu estilo (Natural, Profesional, Prompt, Crudo, Solo transcripción y los tuyos), con un estilo por app.
  • Traducción a 34 idiomas con Ctrl+Shift+Y, y una tarjeta con chips para rehacer el texto en otro estilo o idioma.
  • Comando (Ctrl+Alt+K): selecciona un texto, di qué hacer y el resultado reemplaza la selección.
  • Unos 100 idiomas para hablar; la configuración y la barra están en español, inglés, portugués, francés, alemán, japonés, chino, ruso, hindi y bengalí.
  • Varios proveedores (Groq, Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, OpenAI o un servidor compatible con OpenAI): si uno falla, se usa el siguiente, y si la transcripción falla, la grabación se guarda para reintentar sin volver a hablar.

Para empezar: crea una clave gratis en console.groq.com/keys; la primera vez se abre un asistente rápido. Luego haz clic en un campo de texto, pulsa Ctrl+Shift+Espacio, habla y vuelve a pulsarlo. Esc cancela. "Pegar de nuevo" y "Dictar ahora" están en el menú del icono del área de notificación.

Privacidad: el audio va solo al proveedor de voz que configuraste, solo con una clave guardada (mientras hablas, para la vista previa en vivo, y al parar); el texto va al proveedor de texto, con el nombre de la app en la que escribes y las palabras de tu diccionario, y con el Comando también va el texto seleccionado. Si Groq responde que el modelo elegido ya no existe, el mod pide su lista de modelos y prueba hasta 4 con una prueba corta. Rige la política de privacidad de cada proveedor. No se guarda nada en disco: si una transcripción falla, la grabación queda solo en memoria (las 3 últimas). Las claves se guardan cifradas para tu cuenta de Windows. Limitaciones: no escribe en apps abiertas como administrador (el texto queda copiado), el Comando no funciona en terminales, solo usa proveedores en la nube y necesita internet, y una grabación se detiene sola a los 12 minutos.
